metadata.title: feat(helm): standalone Postgres + PgBouncer for OCP
metadata.author: gandhipratik203

description:
## Summary

Removes the CrunchyData PGO operator dependency for OCP deployments. The Helm chart can now deploy the full stack — Postgres, PgBouncer, Redis, NGINX, Gateway — with a single `helm install`. No operator installation, no custom resources, no cluster-admin prerequisites beyond the namespace.

Uses the CrunchyData `crunchy-pgbouncer` image from the Red Hat Ecosystem Catalog for connection pooling. PgBouncer credentials are stored in a Kubernetes Secret for production readiness. All template changes are backwards-compatible and gated by values — existing deployments are unaffected.

Validated on OCP 4.20 with 3 gateway replicas. MCP benchmark achieved **317 RPS** without plugins and **306 RPS** with plugins enforced, both at **0% failures** on fresh-session operations.

---

## Gap closed

**The OCP deployment required an external operator before you could `helm install`.**

PR #4053 introduced OCP support using the CrunchyData PGO operator for managed Postgres. While that provides HA and automated backups, it introduces a hard dependency: you need cluster-admin access to install the operator, it may conflict with existing operators, and it adds operational overhead that not every team wants or needs.

This PR closes that gap by making the Helm chart fully self-contained on OCP. The chart's built-in Postgres and PgBouncer (with a Red Hat certified image) handle the database layer without any operator. The trade-off is explicit: no automatic HA or managed backups — but the deployment is a single command.

| | Before (PGO, PR #4053) | After (this PR) |
|--|----------------------|-----------------|
| **Prerequisites** | Install PGO operator + apply PostgresCluster CR | None (just `helm install`) |
| **Cluster-admin needed** | Yes (operator install) | No |
| **Postgres** | Operator-managed (HA, WAL archiving, failover) | Helm Deployment (single pod) |
| **PgBouncer** | Operator-managed sidecar | `crunchy-pgbouncer` (Red Hat catalog) |
| **Backups** | pgBackRest (automated) | Manual |
| **When to use** | Production with HA requirements | Dev/test, POCs, or teams without operator access |

Both approaches coexist — different service names, different secrets, no conflicts. Teams can start with the standalone approach and graduate to PGO when they need HA.

Full deployment guide: [`docs/docs/deployment/openshift-helm.md`](https://github.com/IBM/mcp-context-forge/blob/ocp-standalone-postgres/docs/docs/deployment/openshift-helm.md)

---

## Architecture

### Standalone deployment topology

```text
                         ┌─────────────┐
                         │   Client     │
                         └──────┬───────┘
                                │ HTTPS
                                ▼
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  OCP Cluster                                                              │
│                                                                           │
│  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐  │
│  │  OCP Router (HAProxy)                                                │  │
│  │  TLS termination: edge or re-encrypt                                │  │
│  └────────────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────────────┘  │
│                                   │                                       │
│  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐  │
│  │  NGINX Proxy (UBI9)                                                  │  │
│  │  1 pod × 4 CPU  |  Port 8080 (HTTP), 8443 (TLS)  |  32K conns      │  │
│  └────────────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────────────┘  │
│                                   │                                       │
│  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐  │
│  │  ContextForge Gateway                                                │  │
│  │  3 pods × 8 CPU  |  Gunicorn 8 workers  |  Python MCP core          │  │
│  │  Session pool enabled  |  Cache TTLs 300s                            │  │
│  └───┬──────────────────┬──────────────────────────────────────────────┘  │
│      │                  │                                                  │
│      ▼                  ▼                                                  │
│  ┌──────────────┐  ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────┐    │
│  │  Redis        │  │  PgBouncer (crunchy-pgbouncer)                 │    │
│  │  7-alpine     │  │  Red Hat certified  |  transaction pooling     │    │
│  │  2 CPU, 2Gi   │  │  3000 max clients  |  120 pool size           │    │
│  └──────────────┘  └────────────────────────┬───────────────────────┘    │
│                                              │                            │
│                                              ▼                            │
│                    ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────┐    │
│                    │  PostgreSQL 17 (standalone)                      │    │
│                    │  Helm-managed Deployment  |  emptyDir storage    │    │
│                    │  4 CPU, 4Gi  |  Non-root compatible              │    │
│                    └─────────────────────────────────────────────────┘    │
│                                                                           │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

### PGO approach vs Standalone approach

```text
PGO (PR #4053):                          Standalone (this PR):

  Gateway ──► PGO PgBouncer ──► PGO PG     Gateway ──► Helm PgBouncer ──► Helm PG
                  │                                          │
            Managed by CrunchyData              Managed by Helm chart
            operator (HA, backups,              (single pod, emptyDir,
             auto-failover)                      no auto-failover)
```

---

## Comparison with PGO approach

| Aspect | PGO (PR #4053) | Standalone (this PR) |
|--------|---------------|---------------------|
| Postgres | Operator-managed (HA, WAL archiving) | Helm Deployment (single pod) |
| PgBouncer | Operator-managed sidecar | `crunchy-pgbouncer` (Red Hat catalog) |
| Setup | Install operator + CR + Helm | Just Helm |
| HA / Failover | Automatic | None |
| Backups | pgBackRest (automated) | Manual |
| Coexistence | Both can run in same namespace | Different service names, no conflicts |

---

## Test results

<details>
<summary>MCP benchmark — without plugins (3 gateway pods, 125 users, 60s)</summary>

**Configuration:**
- 3 gateway pods (8 CPU, Gunicorn 8 workers each)
- 1 NGINX pod (UBI9, 4 CPU)
- 1 PgBouncer pod (crunchy-pgbouncer, transaction mode)
- 1 Postgres pod (postgres:17, emptyDir)
- 1 Redis pod (7-alpine, persistent)
- Locust: 1 master + 1 worker

**Results (fresh-session MCP operations):**

| Endpoint | Requests | Failures | Avg | Med |
|----------|----------|----------|-----|-----|
| MCP initialize | 1,849 | 0 (0%) | 31ms | 22ms |
| MCP tools/list | 1,849 | 0 (0%) | 38ms | 32ms |
| **Total** | **3,698** | **0 (0%)** | **35ms** | **28ms** |

**317 RPS, 0% failures, 35ms avg latency**

</details>

<details>
<summary>MCP benchmark — with plugins enforced (3 gateway pods, 125 users, 60s)</summary>

**Plugins in enforce mode:** RateLimiterPlugin (10000/m), OutputLengthGuardPlugin, SecretsDetectionPlugin. Other plugins in permissive.

**Results (fresh-session MCP operations):**

| Endpoint | Requests | Failures | Avg | Med |
|----------|----------|----------|-----|-----|
| MCP initialize | 2,474 | 0 (0%) | 36ms | 24ms |
| MCP tools/list | 2,473 | 0 (0%) | 45ms | 35ms |
| **Total** | **4,947** | **0 (0%)** | **40ms** | **32ms** |

**306 RPS, 0% failures, 40ms avg latency**

</details>

<details>
<summary>Plugin overhead comparison</summary>

| Config | Pods | RPS | Avg Latency | Med Latency | Failures |
|--------|------|-----|-------------|-------------|----------|
| Without plugins | 3 | 317 | 35ms | 28ms | 0% |
| With plugins (enforce) | 3 | 306 | 40ms | 32ms | 0% |

Plugins add ~5ms latency with **0% failures**. Consistent with the PGO benchmark observation that the plugin pipeline does not degrade performance.

</details>

---

## Issues resolved for CrunchyData PgBouncer on OCP

<details>
<summary>1. CrashLoopBackOff — no config file</summary>

**Symptom:** PgBouncer pod starts and exits immediately with no logs.

**Root cause:** `crunchy-pgbouncer` is raw PgBouncer — does not accept env vars like `edoburu/pgbouncer`. Requires `pgbouncer.ini` at `/etc/pgbouncer/`. Default config has `listen_addr = localhost`, empty `[databases]`, and `logfile = /var/log/pgbouncer/` (permission denied under OCP arbitrary UID).

**Fix:** Created `configmap-pgbouncer.yaml` with templated `pgbouncer.ini` using `/tmp` for writable paths and `listen_addr = 0.0.0.0`.

</details>

<details>
<summary>2. Readiness probe failure — no pg_isready binary</summary>

**Symptom:** PgBouncer pod stays `0/1 Running`. Gateway cannot reach PgBouncer (no Service endpoints).

**Root cause:** Default probes use `pg_isready` which doesn't exist in the minimal `crunchy-pgbouncer` image.

**Fix:** Override probes to use TCP socket checks (`type: tcp`, `port: 6432`) in values.

</details>

<details>
<summary>3. Password authentication failed</summary>

**Symptom:** PgBouncer logs `password authentication failed for user "admin"`. Gateway stuck at DB probe.

**Root cause:** `auth_type = trust` doesn't capture or forward the client password to the Postgres backend.

**Fix:** Changed to `auth_type = plain` with credentials in `userlist.txt` (stored in a Kubernetes Secret, not ConfigMap).

</details>

<details>
<summary>4. Helm release stuck in "failed"</summary>

**Symptom:** `helm list` shows failed. Cannot `helm upgrade`.

**Root cause:** `register-fast-test` post-install hook times out (fast-test-server ImagePullBackOff from OCP shared registry).

**Fix:** Use `--no-hooks` during install. Register servers manually after.

</details>

---

## Limitations

1. **No HA or automatic failover** — Postgres runs as a single Helm-managed pod. If the pod goes down, it restarts but there is no standby replica for zero-downtime failover. For production HA, use the PGO approach (PR #4053).

2. **Ephemeral storage** — Postgres uses `emptyDir` by default (data is lost on pod restart). Persistent storage requires a PVC with an available storage class or pre-provisioned NFS PV.

3. **No automated backups** — Unlike PGO (which provides pgBackRest with WAL archiving and scheduled backups), this approach requires manual backup procedures.

4. **Two-step Helm install** — Same as the PGO approach: Alembic migration contention requires installing with `replicaCount=1` first, then scaling up after migration completes.

5. **PgBouncer auth_type plain** — `userlist.txt` stores the Postgres password in plain text (inside a Kubernetes Secret). For stronger auth, a future iteration could use `scram-sha-256` with hashed credentials.

commits.message:
feat(helm): preliminary OCP deployment with CrunchyData PGO and MCP benchmark

Add OpenShift deployment support using an externally managed PostgreSQL
operator (CrunchyData PGO). The standard Helm chart assumes root container
access and Helm-managed Postgres/PgBouncer, which are blocked by OpenShift's
restricted-v2 SCC.

Changes:
- NGINX unprivileged support: pid /tmp/nginx.pid, configurable containerPort
  (default 80), TLS listener gated by nginxProxy.tls.enabled
- OpenShift Route template (route-ocp.yaml): external access via OCP HAProxy
  router, supports edge and re-encrypt TLS termination
- External Postgres support: postgres.external.enabled with configurable
  secret key mappings for operator-provided credentials
- Redis configmap: remove inline comments from save directives (bug fix)
- OCP values file (values-ocp-pgo.yaml): tuned for 3 gateway replicas with
  Gunicorn 8 workers, session pool, 300s cache TTLs, connection pools
- CrunchyData PostgresCluster CR with tuned shared_buffers and PgBouncer
- MCP benchmark results: 371 RPS, 0% failures with Python core

All template changes are backwards-compatible via value gates that default
to off. Non-OCP deployments are unaffected.

Closes #4052

Signed-off-by: Pratik Gandhi <gandhipratik203@gmail.com>

fix(helm): move Redis save comments to own lines and update secrets baseline

Redis does not support inline comments on config directives
(see https://github.com/redis/redis/issues/521). Move save directive
comments to their own lines to prevent config parse errors.
Also update .secrets.baseline for values-ocp-pgo.yaml entry.

commits.message:
feat(helm): switch OCP NGINX to Red Hat UBI9 certified image

Replace Alpine-based nginx-unprivileged with Red Hat UBI9 NGINX
(registry.access.redhat.com/ubi9/nginx-126) for OCP deployments.
Addresses supply chain concerns with Alpine base images.

- Add configurable command override in NGINX deployment template
  (gated by nginxProxy.command, no impact on other deployments)
- Set command: ["nginx", "-g", "daemon off;"] in OCP values to
  bypass the UBI image's S2I entrypoint
- Benchmarked: 356 RPS, 0% failures (identical to Alpine baseline)

Signed-off-by: Pratik Gandhi <gandhipratik203@gmail.com>
commits.author: Pratik Gandhi

commits.message:
feat(helm): standalone Postgres + CrunchyData PgBouncer for OCP

Add OCP deployment path that uses the chart's built-in Postgres and
PgBouncer instead of requiring the CrunchyData PGO operator.

- Add values-ocp.yaml with standalone Postgres (postgres:17) and
  crunchy-pgbouncer from Red Hat catalog
- Add configmap-pgbouncer.yaml template for config-file-based PgBouncer
  images (gated by pgbouncer.useConfigFile, backwards compatible)
- Add command override support to PgBouncer deployment template
- Add volume mounts for pgbouncer.ini and userlist.txt
- Add DEPLOY-OCP-STANDALONE.md with full deployment guide and
  troubleshooting for crunchy-pgbouncer on OCP restricted SCC

Tested on OCP 4.20: 3 gateway pods, crunchy-pgbouncer transaction
pooling, all pods healthy.

Signed-off-by: Pratik Gandhi <gandhipratik203@gmail.com>

commits.message:
fix(helm): move PgBouncer userlist.txt from ConfigMap to Secret

The userlist.txt contains the Postgres password in plain text.
ConfigMaps are stored unencrypted in etcd; Secrets support encryption
at rest. Move userlist.txt to a dedicated Secret and mount it
read-only in the PgBouncer pod.
